content.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `tools/fa-clip/` — the native macOS pasteboard helper (gh-2040): a plain
  `NSPasteboard` reader (`fa-clip <png|jpeg|tiff>` → bytes on stdout, exit
  2 = flavor absent), built by `scripts/build_fa_clip.sh` into the macOS
  CLI bundles (`bundle/bin/fa-clip`, per-arch) and shipped beside the `fa`
  binary — install.sh, install_local.sh and the self-update swap all copy
  it. The CLI resolves it relative to its own executable, never PATH; a
  missing/broken helper degrades to the named pasteboard-unavailable path.
  NEVER reintroduce the AppleScript/Apple Events clipboard transport
  (`osascript` is grep-gated out of `bin/` + `lib/src/cli/` —
  test/cli/fa_clip_helper_test.dart); the TCC «access data from other
  apps» dialog class must stay dead. macOS text reads stay on `pbpaste`
  (already prompt-free — documented split, gh-2040 AC4).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics. Self-signal immunity
  (gh-1763): POSIX scripts are delivered from a per-exec private temp
  file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — prelude restores `sh -c`
  positional-param parity, so `$0`/`$#`/exit codes/`set -e`/stdin are
  unchanged; legacy `sh -c <command>` fallback when the temp dir cannot
  be created) so the wrapper argv never carries the script body —
  `pkill -f <pat>` inside a command cannot match its own shell; a
  provisioned-once guard (`lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`) puts
  `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims at the head of PATH plus a `kill()`
  prelude function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group
  (exported as `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`, overridable per exec via
  `ShellExecOptions.env` for tests) and the invoking shell, while
  legitimate victims stay killable; Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
  Residual caveat: shapes the shim cannot model — output modes
  (`-c`, `-v`, `-l`, `-a`, `--count`, any other long option), a signal
  spelled after the pattern, extra operands, or a selection pgrep
  rejects — exec the real, unshimed binary and are NOT covered by the
  exemption (keep the pattern away from the harness cmdline in those
  spellings).
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  gh-1934 (413-proof sessions): image blocks OUTSIDE the kept region —
  first seen before the LAST renumbering boundary — evict to
  `[image dropped: <key8>]` placeholders (payload-only, JSONL
  byte-identical); kept-region images ride on under the normal caps; the 413 recovery ladder
  (`agent_loop_image_recovery.dart` + `image_recovery.dart`, bounded at
  2 passes per response, each 413 halving the session's adaptive
  `images.maxBytesPerRequest`) drops the oldest images (pass 1), then
  strips ALL images including the current message (pass 2, latched
  session-wide), carrying the `[images] recovered from 413:` notice +
  model-visible note; classification lives in `image_overflow.dart`
  (`isPayloadTooLargeError`), surface wording in `image_drop_ux.dart`
  (`ImageDropReason.evicted`).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape (no eviction, no ladder). `agent_loop.dart` applies it in
  `_buildRequestContext` after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing
  repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +

## PR Description

Fixes #2160

## Diagnosis (diff-region analysis)

Downloaded golden-failure-diffs 14009835006 (run 43361333542, head 9a0fa0f3) and mined the nightly release leg (run 43358328610, job 131665590383 — no diff artifact, log only). **Every failure on both legs carries the identical signature: 0.01% / 40px**, and the debug diff images show the region exactly: the composer's 2×20px **text caret** (testImage renders `|Type a message`, master golden has no caret). 40px = 2px caret width × 20px caret height; nothing else on these tiles is 40px. Confirmed by a pixel probe on flutter 3.50.0: a caret-on capture vs a caret-free capture of the same bubble tile differs by **exactly 40px**.

**Mechanism.** `ChatComposer` autofocusses its field (post-frame `requestFocus`); with Material 3 defaults the caret runs EditableText's infinite iOS blink simulation, which re-arms itself through zero-duration timers (`_onCursorTick` → `Timer(Duration.zero)` → `animateWith`). Whether the caret is mid-ON-phase at capture depends on how many timer hops elapsed before the snapshot — wall-clock dependent when the tile is pumped inside `tester.runAsync` (the binding forks a real-timer zone there, flutter_test binding.dart:2387-2402), and loop-count dependent in the mount-wait loops. Fast Mac dev boxes land a consistent off-phase (always green); loaded CI hosts and the release nightly land random phases per tile/run (intermittent debug reds; the release leg failed 5 bubble tiles + generated-media in one run while sibling tiles passed — timing luck, not a raster delta). This also explains `fix/2138` (#2141 cycles) going 4/4 red on the same tile: the phase at capture was host-deterministic on that head.

**Why the existing guard didn't hold.** `disableComposerCaret` (#2112) unfocuses, sets `canRequestFocus=false` (refocus is impossible — the right idea), then pumps **zero duration**. The capture (`matchesGoldenFile` → `captureImage` → `binding.runAsync`) can then race the blink's pending real-zone re-arm; a caret at partial opacity still diffs ~40px. And `chat_generated_media` never had any caret handling at all — it fails in both legs.

## Fix (test-only, 1 file, +33/−8)

Mirrors the in-repo precedent that has **zero sightings across all legs** — the generated-image shot already does unfocus + `pump(600ms)` + `pump()`:

1. `disableComposerCaret`: after unfocus + `canRequestFocus=false`, pump 600ms (past the 500ms blink half-period) and render one more frame, then assert `cursorCurrentlyVisible == false` for every `EditableText` — a future framework change now fails loudly instead of drifting goldens silently.
2. `chat_generated_media`: call `disableComposerCaret` before the capture (it was the only chat-family tile with none).

After unfocus, `_stopCursorBlink` zeroes the caret opacity instantly and cancels the pending re-arm timer; `canRequestFocus=false` blocks every late post-frame `requestFocus` forever. The captured frame is caret-free by construction — in debug and release, at any blink phase.

**No rebaseline needed**: the committed baselines are already caret-free (proven by the passing CI runs of the same tiles and by the 5× local runs below — zero golden PNGs touched).

## Proof

- flutter **3.50.0** (exact CI pin), `TZ=UTC`, worktree standalone SDK.
- `flutter test test/golden/chat_golden_test.dart` — **5/5 runs, all 15 tests green, zero variance**; `git status` after the runs shows only the test file modified (baselines byte-stable).
- `dart format` clean on the touched file; `dart analyze` shows only the two pre-existing infos (deprecated material import, local `_pumpAttachmentBubble` naming) already on main.
- Pixel probe (throwaway, deleted): caret-on vs caret-free diff = exactly 40px, matching every CI signature; production helper at blink-phase 0 (caret visibly ON before unfocus) leaves 0 leaking pixels after the fix's pump hop.

## Delivered vs remaining

- Delivered: root-cause determinism fix covering both the intermittent debug reds and the release-mode 6-file red (one mechanism — the caret — explains both; per-test tolerance / release-leg baseline policy not needed, and the repo has no tolerance precedent to mirror).
- Remaining: none for the chat_golden_test family. If a future red presents a *different* 40px region, that's a new diagnosis — the loud `cursorCurrentlyVisible` assert plus the caret-free capture make a caret recurrence impossible on this surface.

# pr-2164: fix(2160): pin composer caret determinism in chat goldens

## Description

Fixes #2160

## Diagnosis (diff-region analysis)

Downloaded golden-failure-diffs 14009835006 (run 43361333542, head 9a0fa0f3) and mined the nightly release leg (run 43358328610, job 131665590383 — no diff artifact, log only). **Every failure on both legs carries the identical signature: 0.01% / 40px**, and the debug diff images show the region exactly: the composer's 2×20px **text caret** (testImage renders `|Type a message`, master golden has no caret). 40px = 2px caret width × 20px caret height; nothing else on these tiles is 40px. Confirmed by a pixel probe on flutter 3.50.0: a caret-on capture vs a caret-free capture of the same bubble tile differs by **exactly 40px**.

**Mechanism.** `ChatComposer` autofocusses its field (post-frame `requestFocus`); with Material 3 defaults the caret runs EditableText's infinite iOS blink simulation, which re-arms itself through zero-duration timers (`_onCursorTick` → `Timer(Duration.zero)` → `animateWith`). Whether the caret is mid-ON-phase at capture depends on how many timer hops elapsed before the snapshot — wall-clock dependent when the tile is pumped inside `tester.runAsync` (the binding forks a real-timer zone there, flutter_test binding.dart:2387-2402), and loop-count dependent in the mount-wait loops. Fast Mac dev boxes land a consistent off-phase (always green); loaded CI hosts and the release nightly land random phases per tile/run (intermittent debug reds; the release leg failed 5 bubble tiles + generated-media in one run while sibling tiles passed — timing luck, not a raster delta). This also explains `fix/2138` (#2141 cycles) going 4/4 red on the same tile: the phase at capture was host-deterministic on that head.

**Why the existing guard didn't hold.** `disableComposerCaret` (#2112) unfocuses, sets `canRequestFocus=false` (refocus is impossible — the right idea), then pumps **zero duration**. The capture (`matchesGoldenFile` → `captureImage` → `binding.runAsync`) can then race the blink's pending real-zone re-arm; a caret at partial opacity still diffs ~40px. And `chat_generated_media` never had any caret handling at all — it fails in both legs.

## Fix (test-only, 1 file, +33/−8)

Mirrors the in-repo precedent that has **zero sightings across all legs** — the generated-image shot already does unfocus + `pump(600ms)` + `pump()`:

1. `disableComposerCaret`: after unfocus + `canRequestFocus=false`, pump 600ms (past the 500ms blink half-period) and render one more frame, then assert `cursorCurrentlyVisible == false` for every `EditableText` — a future framework change now fails loudly instead of drifting goldens silently.
2. `chat_generated_media`: call `disableComposerCaret` before the capture (it was the only chat-family tile with none).

After unfocus, `_stopCursorBlink` zeroes the caret opacity instantly and cancels the pending re-arm timer; `canRequestFocus=false` blocks every late post-frame `requestFocus` forever. The captured frame is caret-free by construction — in debug and release, at any blink phase.

**No rebaseline needed**: the committed baselines are already caret-free (proven by the passing CI runs of the same tiles and by the 5× local runs below — zero golden PNGs touched).

## Proof

- flutter **3.50.0** (exact CI pin), `TZ=UTC`, worktree standalone SDK.
- `flutter test test/golden/chat_golden_test.dart` — **5/5 runs, all 15 tests green, zero variance**; `git status` after the runs shows only the test file modified (baselines byte-stable).
- `dart format` clean on the touched file; `dart analyze` shows only the two pre-existing infos (deprecated material import, local `_pumpAttachmentBubble` naming) already on main.
- Pixel probe (throwaway, deleted): caret-on vs caret-free diff = exactly 40px, matching every CI signature; production helper at blink-phase 0 (caret visibly ON before unfocus) leaves 0 leaking pixels after the fix's pump hop.

## Delivered vs remaining

- Delivered: root-cause determinism fix covering both the intermittent debug reds and the release-mode 6-file red (one mechanism — the caret — explains both; per-test tolerance / release-leg baseline policy not needed, and the repo has no tolerance precedent to mirror).
- Remaining: none for the chat_golden_test family. If a future red presents a *different* 40px region, that's a new diagnosis — the loud `cursorCurrentlyVisible` assert plus the caret-free capture make a caret recurrence impossible on this surface.

# Review Policy

Preset: `default` — resolved from: built-in default (resolution chain: projectConfig.reviewPolicy → workflow jobParams → built-in default).
Verification: `none` — findings post exactly as the review leg raised them — no second-stage verification.
Every verdict on this PR is traceable to this table.

| Severity | Round | Fix | Gates approval |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🚨 BLOCKING | rework | mandatory | YES |
| ⚠️ IMPORTANT | rework | mandatory | YES |
| 💡 SUGGESTION | polish | mandatory | no |
| 🪶 NIT | none | opportunistic | no |

Verification: `none` — findings post exactly as the review leg raised them — no second-stage verification.

Bounds: polishMaxThreads=6 · polishMaxChangedLines=80 · opportunisticMaxThreads=8 · opportunisticSameFilesOnly=true · densityMin=2 · densityMax=8 · sweepBatch=10 · sweepMaxAgeDays=30

Density cap (💡/🪶 threads only; 🚨/⚠️ never capped): allowed = clamp(round(2 + 3*sqrt(additions/200)), 2, 8).
Rank your findings and post the top-K as threads; the overflow becomes a ranked digest list in the general comment. The census counts posted threads + digest lines.

Machine enforcement: the approval is recomputed from the severity census + this policy — the model verdict is advisory. Any 🚨 or ⚠️ open → REQUEST_CHANGES; only 💡/🪶 → APPROVE.
## Downgrade protocol

A rework lap may downgrade a specific ⚠️ IMPORTANT finding to 💡 SUGGESTION **only with a written justification** in the census (the thread reply and the response summary: why this is not maintainability debt). A silent downgrade does not exist: the next review round re-raises it as ⚠️ IMPORTANT and the cycle repeats. A justified downgrade lets a false-⚠️ review converge to APPROVE without a code change.

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's

logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →

arguments.content:
💡 **SUGGESTION: blink-mechanism attribution — the iOS caret simulation is not what these tiles run**

The new comment says the caret is *"EditableText's iOS caret simulation [which] re-arms itself through zero-duration timers"*. Verified against the exact SDK this CI pins (flutter 3.50.0): Material's `TextField` enables that simulation **only on `TargetPlatform.iOS`** — `cursorOpacityAnimates ??= true` is the iOS case of the platform switch in `TextField.build` (text_field.dart:1597); the **macOS** case resolves `??= false` (text_field.dart:1616-1620), as do Linux/Windows/Android. The app never overrides it (no `cursorOpacityAnimates` anywhere in `fa_ui`/`flutter_app`), and these tiles set no `debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride`.

The golden CI leg (`flutter-app-goldens` in ci.yml) runs on `macos-latest`, so what these captures actually race is the **step blink**: `_startCursorBlink` arms `Timer.periodic(_kCursorBlinkHalfPeriod)` (editable_text.dart:4913) and `_onCursorTick` toggles the opacity 1↔0 directly — the `animateWith(_iosBlinkCursorSimulation)` + `Timer(Duration.zero)` re-arm chain is never entered. The timer is created in whatever zone is active when focus lands — inside `tester.runAsync` that is the binding's real-timer fork (binding.dart:2389), so the ON/OFF phase at capture is wall-clock dependent, exactly as the comment concludes.

**The fix itself is mechanism-agnostic and correct** — unfocus zeroes the opacity (`_stopCursorBlink`), `canRequestFocus=false` blocks every late re-focus, the 600ms hop renders a caret-free frame, and the loud `cursorCurrentlyVisible` assert makes a framework change fail instead of drifting: all verified against the 3.50.0 source, and the assert passed on all 6 helper invocations in this review's sandbox run. But this helper comment is the file's canonical flake-diagnosis reference (the same claim also sits in the PR/ticket description), and the next caret red will send whoever reads it chasing the iOS-only `animateWith` path these tiles never execute. Suggest rewording, e.g.:

> The caret blink is an infinite timer-driven animation. On the platforms CI runs (macOS/Linux hosts, no platform override) Material resolves `cursorOpacityAnimates` to false, so `EditableText` toggles the caret with a `Timer.periodic(kCursorBlinkHalfPeriod)` created wherever focus landed — inside `tester.runAsync` that is the real-timer fork, so the phase at capture is wall-clock dependent. (The iOS-only `cursorOpacityAnimates=true` path re-arms through zero-duration timers instead — same indeterminism, different mechanism.)

## Review Summary — PR #2164 (fix/2160-golden-flake)

**Verdict: APPROVE** — test-only determinism fix for the #2160 golden flakes, no blocking or important findings.

**What I verified (against the pinned flutter 3.50.0 SDK source, not just the diff):**
- The fix mechanism is airtight: `_stopCursorBlink` zeroes the caret opacity on unfocus, `canRequestFocus=false` blocks every late post-frame `requestFocus`, the 600ms hop (> the 500ms `_kCursorBlinkHalfPeriod`) renders a caret-free frame, and the new `cursorCurrentlyVisible` assert makes future framework changes fail loudly instead of drifting goldens.
- The new assert passed on **all 6 helper invocations** in this review's sandbox run.
- Sandbox golden runs drift on linux vs the macOS-captured baselines — **byte-identical failure sets at base and head** (same 14 tiles, same percentages/pixel counts) prove the drift is environmental, not PR-related; baselines stayed untouched in both runs.

Same indeterminism conclusion, wrong mechanism named (also mirrored in the PR/ticket description).
- Two digest notes (general comment): the generated-image tile still uses the weaker inline caret-kill (no `canRequestFocus=false` guard/assert), and five out-of-diff golden files use the unfocus-only pattern.
